entries.name: Common cottongrass
entries.flowers: white cotton tufts, early summer
entries.fruit: small achene in a fluffy seed head
entries.fire: killed to ground; regrows from rhizomes
entries.voxel_shape: grassy tuft with 2-6 nodding white cotton heads on thin stalks
entries.notes: The white dots that turn wet tundra to a meadow in June. Rhizome mats colonise drained pools fast.

entries.name: Tussock cottongrass
entries.flowers: single white cotton tuft per shoot, late spring
entries.fruit: achene in a dense cotton head
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from dense tussock base
entries.voxel_shape: dense dark green tussock hummock with one cotton head each
entries.notes: Builds the classic tussock hummocks: a bouncing, knee-high terrain skin over wet peat.

entries.name: Bigelow's sedge
entries.leaves: fine grass-like leaves in small hummocks
entries.flowers: small brown spikes, early summer
entries.fruit: small nutlet in a bottle-shaped bract
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from base
entries.voxel_shape: low dense sedge hummock, greyer than grass
entries.notes: The default green carpet of arctic-alpine heath; forms low hummocks that read well as ground texture.

entries.name: Tufted hairgrass
entries.leaves: bright glossy tussock leaves with rough edges
entries.flowers: silvery airy panicles, midsummer
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from base
entries.voxel_shape: dense bright green tussock with a shimmering seed cloud above it
entries.notes: Wants damp hollows; the tallest grass of the tundra and an easy wind-animation target.

entries.name: Spiked snow-grass
entries.flowers: tiny spike, midsummer
entries.fire: not applicable; polar desert
entries.voxel_shape: sparse tiny grass spikes in bare frost ground
entries.notes: A pioneer of raw frost-shattered ground in high arctic polar deserts; the first green on new till.

entries.name: Dwarf birch
entries.leaves: small round toothed leaves, crisp autumn gold
entries.flowers: tiny wind-pollinated catkins, spring
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from rootstock
entries.voxel_shape: low rounded bush of tiny round leaves, dense and knee-high
entries.notes: The dominant shrub of low arctic heath; turns the whole tundra amber in September.

entries.name: Arctic willow
entries.leaves: small glossy leaves held flat to the ground
entries.flowers: silky catkins, midsummer
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from spreading roots
entries.voxel_shape: prostrate creeping mat of shiny leaves flat on the ground
entries.notes: Creeps under the snow and spreads by runners; a single plant can mat many square metres.

entries.name: Grayleaf willow
entries.flowers: silky yellow catkins before leaves
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from base
entries.voxel_shape: waist-high grey thicket of oval leaves
entries.notes: Head-high thickets along sheltered tundra rivers; the shrub that turns valleys into willow scrub.

entries.name: Woolly willow
entries.flowers: large silky catkins, midsummer
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from base
entries.voxel_shape: low bushy shrub with visibly fuzzy silver leaves
entries.notes: The felt-leafed willow of rocky arctic slopes; the leaves look frosted even when dry.

entries.name: Polar willow
entries.flowers: minute reddish catkins, midsummer
entries.fire: not applicable; polar desert
entries.voxel_shape: almost invisible creeping coin-leaf mat among stones
entries.notes: One of the smallest willows on Earth; spreads underground and can cover square metres invisibly.

entries.name: Bearberry
entries.flowers: small white-pink urn flowers, early summer
entries.fruit: red mealy berry eaten by bears and birds
entries.fire: resprouts from spreading rhizomes after fire
entries.voxel_shape: low creeping evergreen mat with bright red berries
entries.notes: Evergreen mats dotted with red berries into winter; a staple of ptarmigan and bears.

entries.name: Black crowberry
entries.flowers: minute purple wind flowers, late spring
entries.fire: resprouts from rhizomes after fire
entries.voxel_shape: low sprawling heather of needle leaves with black berries
entries.notes: The juiciest berry on the barrens; crows and grouse strip it before snowfall.

entries.name: Bog bilberry
entries.flowers: small pink bell flowers, late spring
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from rootstock
entries.voxel_shape: knee-high blueberry thicket with blue dusty fruit
entries.notes: The northern blueberry; in good years tundra slopes are lousy with fruit for a few short weeks.

entries.name: Lingonberry
entries.leaves: small glossy evergreen leaves, dotted beneath
entries.flowers: pink bell flowers, early summer
entries.fire: resprouts from rhizomes after fire
entries.voxel_shape: low evergreen carpet with paired red berries
entries.notes: Tart red keepsake berry of the north; the Scandinavian staple that ripens as the tundra empties.

entries.name: Cloudberry
entries.leaves: wrinkled lobed bramble-like leaves, one per shoot
entries.flowers: white five-petalled flowers, midsummer
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from creeping rhizomes
entries.voxel_shape: low creeping stem with one leaf and one amber berry each
entries.notes: The most prized berry of the north; scarce, perishable, and gone within days of ripening.

entries.name: Bog Labrador tea
entries.leaves: narrow evergreen leaves, rusty felt beneath
entries.flowers: clusters of small white flowers, early summer
entries.fire: resprouts from base after fire
entries.voxel_shape: waist-high shrubby heather with frothy white flower clusters
entries.notes: Rusty-backed evergreen shrub of wet tundra; the leaves steep into a bitter medicinal tea.

entries.name: Arctic bell-heather
entries.leaves: minute scale leaves pressed in four ranks
entries.flowers: nodding white bell flowers, midsummer
entries.fire: killed to ground; very slow to recover
entries.voxel_shape: low frost-cracked mat of mossy bell-heather with white bells
entries.notes: The signature evergreen of high arctic heath; crackles underfoot and holds snow like a moss.

entries.name: Bog rosemary
entries.flowers: nodding pink bells, early summer
entries.fire: resprouts from base after fire
entries.voxel_shape: low grey-blue bog shrub with hanging pink bells
entries.notes: Bog-rosemary flags waterlogged peat: where it grows, the ground is soft and deep.

entries.name: Lapland rosebay
entries.flowers: small purple-magenta funnel flowers, midsummer
entries.fire: killed to ground; slow to recover
entries.voxel_shape: dwarfed curled heather with magenta specks
entries.notes: A true high-arctic dwarf rhododendron; flowering tufts are small enough to hide under one hand.

entries.name: Eight-petal mountain avens
entries.flowers: creamy eight-petalled stars, early summer
entries.fire: killed to ground; mats regrow slowly
entries.voxel_shape: creeping evergreen mat studded with white stars and feathery seed heads
entries.notes: Named after a Greek nymph; its sudden abundance in the fossil record marks ancient cold snaps.

entries.name: Purple saxifrage
entries.leaves: minute overlapping evergreen scales in cushions
entries.flowers: magenta-purple cup flowers, first bloom after snowmelt
entries.fire: not applicable; sparse rocky ground
entries.voxel_shape: dense pink-purple cushion clinging to bare rock
entries.notes: Often the first flower to open in the high arctic; cushions split rock a fraction at a time.

entries.name: Nodding saxifrage
entries.leaves: small rounded kidney leaves in a basal rosette
entries.flowers: rare; tiny reddish bells nodding downward
entries.fruit: almost always tiny bulbils in the leaf axils instead of seed
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from bulbils
entries.voxel_shape: small rosette with a leaning stem of red drop-like bulbils
entries.notes: Skips flowers entirely in most years; clones itself from leaf-axil bulbils instead.

entries.name: Mountain sorrel
entries.flowers: spike of tiny reddish-green flowers, midsummer
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from rootstock
entries.voxel_shape: small clump of round sour leaves with a reddening seed spike
entries.notes: Tastes like thin sorrel; arctic travellers chewed it against scurvy.

entries.name: Alpine bistort
entries.leaves: small oval leaves with wavy edges
entries.flowers: spike of pink-white florets above bulbils, midsummer
entries.fruit: viviparous: lower flowers fall off as bulbils that root directly
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from rhizomes and bulbils
entries.voxel_shape: low rosette with a pink-tipped spike dropping tiny plantlets
entries.notes: Viviparous again: lower 'flowers' are miniature plantlets that drop and root where they land.

entries.name: Moss campion
entries.leaves: minute moss-like evergreen leaves in dense cushions
entries.flowers: deep pink cup flowers dotted on the cushion, midsummer
entries.fire: killed to ground; extremely slow to regrow
entries.voxel_shape: rock-hard domed pincushion of pink flowers
entries.notes: Cushions reach 350 years; growth is a centimetre in a good year, and shrinkage in a bad one.

entries.name: Svalbard poppy
entries.flowers: large yellow-white silky poppy, midsummer
entries.fire: not applicable; polar desert
entries.voxel_shape: hairy stem holding one big papery cup above bare gravel
entries.notes: Svalbard's emblem; a silky white-yellow cup steering toward the low northern sun.

entries.name: Milky draba
entries.flowers: tiny white four-petalled cruciform flowers, midsummer
entries.fire: not applicable; polar desert
entries.voxel_shape: minute white-star clusters over gravel
entries.notes: Shrugs off frost and wind on raw polar desert; a whisper of white over the gravel.

entries.name: Woolly lousewort
entries.flowers: woolly pale-pink to cream hooded spikes, midsummer
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from rootstock
entries.voxel_shape: hairy frosted spike of pale hooded flowers
entries.notes: Looks frosted in July; a favourite of arctic botanists because it barely moves all summer.

entries.name: Arctic daisy
entries.flowers: white daisy with yellow disc, late summer
entries.fire: killed to ground; resprouts from rhizomes
entries.voxel_shape: sturdy white daisy on a thick stem
entries.notes: The unmistakable daisy of the high arctic; one robust flower per sturdy moss-free stem.

entries.name: Field horsetail
entries.leaves: no true leaves; green jointed ridged stems
entries.flowers: none; spore cones on separate pale shoots in spring
entries.fire: resprouts from deep rhizomes after fire
entries.voxel_shape: thin jointed green candles with black-ringed joints
entries.notes: Abrasive silica stems were the original scouring pad; spreads everywhere via deep rhizomes.

entries.name: Reindeer lichen
entries.flowers: none; produces spores at branch tips
entries.fire: killed by fire; recovers over decades
entries.voxel_shape: grey-green mossy coral crust covering dry ground
entries.notes: The winter bread of the reindeer; kilometres of dry ridge glow grey-green with it.

entries.name: Iceland moss
entries.leaves: none; upright brown lobed thallus with curled edges
entries.flowers: none; produces spores
entries.fire: killed by fire; recovers over decades
entries.voxel_shape: rusty brown strap-lichen tufts in windswept mats
entries.notes: Not a moss at all; boiled into a bitter porridge in famines and used for chest complaints.

entries.name: Woolly fringe-moss
entries.flowers: none; spore capsules rare in harsh sites
entries.fruit: spore capsule on a thin seta
entries.fire: killed to ground; recovers over years
entries.voxel_shape: grey hoary carpet over rocks, white when dry
entries.notes: Grey domes over exposed boulders; turns ghost-white when dry and green within minutes of rain.

entries.name: Pleurozium feather-moss
entries.leaves: red stems with overlapping yellow-green feathery leaves
entries.flowers: none; spore capsules in damp summers
entries.fire: killed to ground; recovers over years
entries.voxel_shape: soft red-stemmed feathery carpet
entries.notes: The soft red-stemmed feather carpet of tussock heath; nests get lined with it.

entries.name: Sphagnum bog-moss
entries.flowers: none; spore capsules burst with an audible pop
entries.fire: killed to ground; recovers slowly
entries.voxel_shape: lumpy swollen wet hummocks in green, red and orange
entries.notes: Holds twenty times its weight in water; built the peat that underlies much of the tundra.

entries.name: Orange birch bolete
entries.flowers: none
entries.fruit: stout mushroom with orange cap and black-scabbered white stalk; pores not gills
entries.fire: killed to ground; returns with host shrubs
entries.voxel_shape: orange-capped bolete poking from dwarf birch leaf litter
entries.notes: Fruits under dwarf birch after rain; height_m and its season both belong to the fruiting body only.

entries.name: Fly agaric
entries.flowers: none
entries.fruit: bright red cap with white wart flecks; toxic
entries.fire: killed to ground; returns with host trees
entries.voxel_shape: storybook red-and-white toadstool among birch
entries.notes: The fairy-tale toadstool; symbiont of birch and spruce, toxic, instantly readable in voxel art.

entries.name: Dahurian larch
entries.leaves: deciduous soft needles in dense tufts, gold in autumn
entries.flowers: small male and female cones, spring
entries.fruit: small woody cone with winged seeds
entries.fire: resprouts from base; thick bark resists low fire
entries.voxel_shape: sparse cone-shaped conifer in gold or green, far treeline silhouette
entries.notes: The tree that survives Siberia's -60 C winters; marks the treeline edge where tundra gives way to forest.
